blocks.content: Understanding key terminology is essential for mastering Indian Polity and Governance concepts in competitive examinations.

rows: Terminates a sitting only; done by the Presiding Officer of the House.
Terminates a sitting as well as a session; done by the President/Governor.
Ends the existing life of the House (Lok Sabha/Vidhan Sabha); fresh elections required.

items: Direct questions are frequently asked on the difference between Adjournment, Adjournment Sine Die, Prorogation, and Dissolution.
Zero Hour is unique to the Indian Parliamentary System and is not explicitly defined in the official Rule Book.
Article 123 empowers the President to issue Ordinances, while Article 213 empowers Governors.

blocks.title: Key Takeaways
items: Quorum refers to the minimum number of members required to be present to conduct a meeting of the House (1/10th of total members).
Zero Hour is an Indian parliamentary innovation not mentioned in the Rules of Procedure, starting immediately after the Question Hour.
Prorogation terminates both the sitting and a session of the House, unlike Adjournment which only terminates a sitting.
Ordinances promulgated by the President under Article 123 must be approved by Parliament within 6 weeks from its reassembly.
